items.title: Justice PS Koshy appointed acting Chief Justice of Telangana High Court
items.summary: The Central government on Monday notified the appointment of Justice Puthichira Sam Koshy as the Acting Chief Justice of the Telangana High Court. A notification issued by the Ministry of Law and Justice stated that the President made the appointment in exercise of the power conferred under Article 223 of the Constitution of India. Justice Koshy's appointment comes following the elevation of the incumbent Chief Justice of the Telangana High Court, Justice Aparesh Kumar Singh , as a Judge of the Supreme Court of India. The notification stated that Justice Koshy will assume charge of the office from the date Justice Singh relinquishes charge to take oath at the apex court. Justice Koshy was appointed as an additional judge of the Chhattisgarh High Court in September 2013 and made a permanent judge in March 2016, before being transferred to the Telangana High Court in 2023. [Read Notification]

items.title: Centre appoints Gurvinder Pal Singh as additional judge of Delhi High Court
items.summary: The Central government on Monday notified the appointment of judicial officer Gurvinder Pal Singh as an additional judge of the Delhi High Court. The notification was issued by Union Law and Justice Minister Arjun Ram Meghwal. The appointment comes nearly a month after the Supreme Court Collegium had recommended Singh's appointment along with seven other judicial officers on September 10. The Collegium had recommended eight names for appointment as judges of the Delhi High Court. Singh was the only one among the eight whose appointment had not been notified in the Centre's earlier notification dated September 19. With Singh's appointment on Monday, the Delhi High Court will have 44 judges against its sanctioned strength of 60, leaving 16 vacancies.

items.title: NUSRL Ranchi students hold protest over women's safety and hostel restrictions
items.summary: Students of National University of Study and Research in Law (NUSRL), Ranchi protested on October 3 over women's safety and hostel rules. The protest ran from about 2 AM to 7 AM, with a few faculty members attending. According to sources, it has ended and the issues are being resolved internally. An email sent to the Vice-Chancellor's (VC) office, the Registrar and the Dean listed 14 concerns from the girls' hostel. Students alleged that labourers frequently move through student areas, some inadequately clothed. They claimed workers have begun living in the new library building near residences. They also said that male workers enter the girls' hostel without adequate notice and that the warning bell is hard to hear. They have sought a fixed, notified schedule. Female students have alleged that some recently posted guards stare at them intrusively and have sought sensitisation, supervision and accountability for security staff. Students also said that several areas on campus and outside the gate are poorly lit and lack CCTV cameras. They alleged that female students have faced eve-teasing shortly after leaving the campus. It noted that the relocated electors are forced to submit Form 6 for new enrolment when their Form 8 for address modification is getting rejected. items.title: Justice Nitin Wasudeo Sambre appointed Acting Chief Justice of Delhi High Court
items.summary: Justice Nitin Wasudeo Sambre was appointed as the Acting Chief Justice of the Delhi High Court on Monday. The Union Ministry of Law and Justice issued a notification in this regard after Chief Justice DK Upadhyaya was elevated to the Supreme Court . "In exercise of the power conferred by Article 223 of the Constitution of India, the President is pleased to appoint Shri Justice Nitin Wasudeo Sambre, Judge of the Delhi High Court, to perform the duties of office of the Chief Justice of that High Court with effect from the date Shri Justice Devendra Kumar Upadhyaya relinquishes the charge of the office of Chief Justice consequent upon his elevation as a Judge of the Supreme Court of India,” the ministry said in a notification. Justice Sambre was born on December 19, 1967 at Nagpur. He graduated in law in 1992 from University College of Law, Nagpur. He enrolled as an advocate on August 25, 1992 and started legal career with then Senior Advocate Sharad A Bobde (former Chief Justice of India). items.title: Kumbh fame Monalisa Bhosle gets relief as MP HC sets aside birth record change
items.summary: The Madhya Pradesh High Court has set aside an order cancelling the birth certificate of Monalisa Bhosle, the young woman who became an internet sensation after videos of her selling rudraksha beads at the 2025 Prayag Maha Kumbh went viral. The Indore Bench of the High Court, in an order passed on Wednesday, October 1, held that Monalisa was not given an opportunity to be heard before her birth record was changed. It directed the Chief Municipal Officer (CMO) of Maheshwar in Khargone district to reconsider the matter after giving her an effective opportunity to present her case. The court, however, did not determine whether Monalisa was born in 2008 or 2009, which is at the heart of the legal dispute surrounding her marriage to actor Farman Khan. Instead, it set aside the cancellation order on the ground that it was passed without hearing the person directly affected by it. “It is, thus, trite that any action prejudicial to a citizen, which is taken by the State or public authority without affording him an opportunity of being heard, would be unfair and arbitrary,” Justice Gajendra Singh said. items.title: India’s women are angry, rightfully so | Let Me Explain 168 | Pooja Prasanna
items.summary: India’s women are angry. Those are slogans from thousands of women and students who have taken to the streets in Delhi over the past week, demanding something that should really not have to be a demand: the right to study, work, travel, and simply exist in public without being afraid of sexual violence. The immediate trigger was the gang rape of a 17-year-old girl at Aastha Kunj Park in south Delhi. The response was swift, but not in the way the protesters wanted. Lady Shri Ram College, a women’s college close to the park, was forced to switch to online classes. Delhi authorities wanted to restrict access to public parks after dark, and announced security measures for vulnerable areas- which they should have done much before. And for many women, that is precisely the problem. Because this isn't really about one case, or even one city. It is about a pattern that has become painfully familiar. A woman is assaulted, there is outrage. And sooner or later comes the advice: don’t go there, don’t stay out late, dress differently, carry something for protection, call someone when you reach home. items.title: ‘Any modified Form 6 has not been approved by us’: CJI Surya Kant
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Monday, October 5 clarified that it had not approved the modified Form 6 being used by the Election Commission of India (ECI) during the ongoing Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. Chief Justice of India Surya Kant made the observation while hearing a petition challenging alleged unilateral decisions taken by Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar. “Any modified Form 6 has not been approved by us. Let’s be clear. When the record is produced, we would like to see who has modified,” CJI Surya Kant observed . The clarification comes after the ECI said in a press note on September 26 that the declaration attached to Form 6 for the SIR exercise had been approved by the Supreme Court. “The declaration attached to Form 6 for SIR has been upheld by the Hon’ble Supreme Court. For non-SIR period, the Forms applicable as Rules (Registration of Electors Roles 1960) will be used,” the ECI had said .
